title: Homeostasis, Co-ordination and Response
seo_title: Secondary 4 Biology: Homeostasis, Co-ordination and Response Worksheets (O-Level)
standard_code: O-Level Biology (6093): Homeostasis, Co-ordination and Response
standard_text: Define homeostasis and explain negative feedback; describe the control of body temperature by the skin and the hypothalamus; describe the control of blood glucose by insulin and glucagon and the treatment of diabetes; describe the nervous system, the structure and functions of sensory, relay and motor neurones, reflex arcs and voluntary and reflex actions; describe the structure of the eye, the pupil reflex and accommodation; define a hormone, describe the effects of adrenaline and compare nervous and hormonal control (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Biology 6093 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Biology worksheets on homeostasis, co-ordination and response: negative feedback, temperature control, insulin and glucagon, diabetes, neurones, reflex arcs, the eye and hormones. 100 questions with answers.

body_html:
How to think about it

The body keeps conditions steady by negative feedback.

  • Too hot: sweating, vasodilation. Too cold: shivering, vasoconstriction. The hypothalamus controls these.
  • High blood glucose → insulin → glucose to glycogen. Low → glucagon → glycogen to glucose.
  • Reflex arc: stimulus → receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector.
  • Near object: ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments slacken, lens thicker. Bright light: the pupil becomes smaller.
Example

Blood glucose 10 mmol/L. Hormone?

above normal

lower it

Answer: insulin

Example

Reading close up. Ciliary muscles?

need a thicker lens

Answer: contract

Common mistakes

  • Saying blood vessels move to the skin surface.
  • Saying the lens gets thicker for distant objects.
  • Saying reflexes need the brain to decide.
  • Saying hormones travel along nerves.

faq.q: How does the body cool down?
faq.a: Sweat glands release more sweat, which evaporates and removes heat, and arterioles in the skin dilate so more heat is lost from blood near the surface.

faq.q: What is the difference between insulin and glucagon?
faq.a: Insulin is released when blood glucose is high and makes the liver store glucose as glycogen. Glucagon is released when blood glucose is low and makes the liver convert glycogen to glucose.

faq.q: How does the eye focus on a near object?
faq.a: The ciliary muscles contract, the suspensory ligaments slacken and the lens becomes thicker, so light is refracted more onto the retina.

items.q: In a reflex arc, why is the response so fast?
c: The impulse travels through a short pathway, often only the spinal cord, without conscious thought.
items.e: Reflexes protect the body.

items.q: A person with type 2 diabetes is often advised to exercise and eat less sugar. Why?
